# Marginalia mentions, table deletion, and a theme layer

## Context

Feedback from a user (tryingET) surfaced three problems, two of them bugs:

1. **Marginalia @-mentions drop the name.** Typing `@`, then picking a suggestion **with the mouse**, leaves only the bare `@` — the inserted name never lands. Keyboard selection isn't an alternative because it was never implemented.
2. **Tables can't be fully deleted.** The first row can't be deleted (the second row's button works), and there's no apparent way to remove the table itself.
3. **The palette is hard on the eyes.** The reporter is a light-mode user who doesn't want dark mode — they want *different colors*. There is no theme layer in the app at all today.

Spellcheck was also raised and has been **explicitly dropped from scope** — the browser exposes no API to read squiggles or open the native suggestion menu, so "hands-off spelling by hotkey" would mean shipping our own dictionary engine, which isn't worth it right now.

Two facts shape the whole plan:

- **This is Qwik, not React.** `component$`, `useStore`, `useVisibleTask$`, QRLs. Event handlers ending in `$` are *asynchronously loaded* — that is the direct cause of bug #1, and it's why the theme flash-guard must be an inline `<script>` rather than a provider.
- **The codebase is unusually ready for theming.** 1873 `var(--color-*)` call sites, **zero** Tailwind color utilities, zero arbitrary hex classes, and just 7 tokens carry ~90% of the UI.

---

## 1. Marginalia @-mentions

The `@`-picker is not a TipTap suggestion plugin — it's plain textarea logic in the comments panel. Four separate defects stack up.

**Files:** `src/components/ui/mention-dropdown.tsx`, `src/utils/mentions.ts`, `src/components/comments/comments-panel.tsx` (two call sites: new-note `:508-552`, reply `:842-893`).

### a. The mouse-pick race — the actual reported bug

`mention-dropdown.tsx:33` guards blur with `onMouseDown$={(e) => e.preventDefault()}`. In Qwik that handler is a QRL: on first interaction its chunk is fetched **asynchronously**, so `preventDefault()` runs after the browser has already dispatched the default mousedown. Sequence: mousedown → textarea blurs → `onBlur$` sets `mentionTarget = null` (`comments-panel.tsx:531-533`, `:871-874`) → dropdown unmounts before mouseup → **no `click` event ever fires** → `onSelect$` never runs → text stays `"@"`.

Fix: use Qwik's declarative `preventdefault:mousedown` JSX attribute, which is applied at serialization time and needs no JS. Already the house idiom — `twyne-editor.tsx:3812-3814`, `auth-panel.tsx:504`, `routes/downloads/index.tsx:129`. Put it on the dropdown **container**, not just each button, so clicks on padding don't blur either.

# Marginalia mentions, table deletion, and a theme layer

## Context

Feedback from a user (tryingET) surfaced three problems, two of them bugs:

1. **Marginalia @-mentions drop the name.** Typing `@`, then picking a suggestion **with the mouse**, leaves only the bare `@` — the inserted name never lands. Keyboard selection isn't an alternative because it was never implemented.
2. **Tables can't be fully deleted.** The first row can't be deleted (the second row's button works), and there's no apparent way to remove the table itself.
3. **The palette is hard on the eyes.** The reporter is a light-mode user who doesn't want dark mode — they want *different colors*. There is no theme layer in the app at all today.

Spellcheck was also raised and has been **explicitly dropped from scope** — the browser exposes no API to read squiggles or open the native suggestion menu, so "hands-off spelling by hotkey" would mean shipping our own dictionary engine, which isn't worth it right now.

Two facts shape the whole plan:

- **This is Qwik, not React.** `component$`, `useStore`, `useVisibleTask$`, QRLs. Event handlers ending in `$` are *asynchronously loaded* — that is the direct cause of bug #1, and it's why the theme flash-guard must be an inline `<script>` rather than a provider.
- **The codebase is unusually ready for theming.** 1873 `var(--color-*)` call sites, **zero** Tailwind color utilities, zero arbitrary hex classes, and just 7 tokens carry ~90% of the UI.

---

## 1. Marginalia @-mentions

The `@`-picker is not a TipTap suggestion plugin — it's plain textarea logic in the comments panel. Four separate defects stack up.

**Files:** `src/components/ui/mention-dropdown.tsx`, `src/utils/mentions.ts`, `src/components/comments/comments-panel.tsx` (two call sites: new-note `:508-552`, reply `:842-893`).

### a. The mouse-pick race — the actual reported bug

`mention-dropdown.tsx:33` guards blur with `onMouseDown$={(e) => e.preventDefault()}`. In Qwik that handler is a QRL: on first interaction its chunk is fetched **asynchronously**, so `preventDefault()` runs after the browser has already dispatched the default mousedown. Sequence: mousedown → textarea blurs → `onBlur$` sets `mentionTarget = null` (`comments-panel.tsx:531-533`, `:871-874`) → dropdown unmounts before mouseup → **no `click` event ever fires** → `onSelect$` never runs → text stays `"@"`.

Fix: use Qwik's declarative `preventdefault:mousedown` JSX attribute, which is applied at serialization time and needs no JS. Already the house idiom — `twyne-editor.tsx:3812-3814`, `auth-panel.tsx:504`, `routes/downloads/index.tsx:129`. Put it on the dropdown **container**, not just each button, so clicks on padding don't blur either.

### b. Blur handler is unconditional

Belt-and-braces so this can't regress: in both `onBlur$` handlers, only clear `mentionTarget` when the blur is leaving the mention UI — check `relatedTarget` against a `data-mention-dropdown` container attribute added in `mention-dropdown.tsx`.

### c. No keyboard path exists at all

The textarea `onKeyDown$` handlers (`:522-530`, `:856-870`) only handle `Escape` and `Mod+Enter`. Add an `activeIndex` to the store, handle `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown`/`Enter`/`Tab` (with `preventDefault` so Enter doesn't insert a newline), reset the index on every `onInput$`, and pass `activeIndex` into `MentionDropdown` for highlight styling + `aria-activedescendant`. Mirror the working pattern in `src/components/editor/slash-command-menu.tsx:49-71`.

### d. Mentions only work at end-of-text

`activeMentionQuery` (`mentions.ts:19-22`) matches `/@([A-Za-z]*)$/` against the whole value, and `applyMention` (`:25-27`) replaces the *last* match. So mid-text mentions never trigger, and editing earlier in a note rewrites the wrong `@`.

Change both to be caret-aware: `activeMentionQuery(value, caret)` matches against `value.slice(0, caret)`; `applyMention(value, name, caret)` returns `{ text, caret }` so the callers can restore the cursor after the inserted name. Widen the character class beyond `[A-Za-z]` to cover digits/hyphens.

> **Check during implementation:** whether persona names contain spaces. If they do, `filterMentionables`' `startsWith` and `mentionedIn`'s `@Name\b` regex are both already broken for those names — flag it, don't silently expand scope.

**Tests:** extend the existing `src/utils/mentions.test.ts` with caret-aware cases (mention mid-sentence, two `@`s in one note, caret position after insert). Add an active-item story to `src/components/ui/mention-dropdown.stories.tsx`.

## 2. Tables

### a. First row not deletable — finish the in-progress fix

This is **not** an availability bug. `getTableActionAvailability` (`extensions/table-format.ts:525-544`) mirrors `editor.can().deleteRow()`, which ProseMirror implements as `isInTable(state)` — essentially always true. The button is enabled and the command works.

The real cause is that **the cell-format panel physically covers row 1**. The committed code renders it at `store.tableToolbar.position.top + 120` (`twyne-editor.tsx:3656-3659`). The toolbar is normally placed `"above"` with `desiredTop = anchor.top - height - gap` where height=112, gap=8 — so `position.top ≈ anchor.top - 120`, putting the panel's top at exactly `anchor.top`, on the first row, at `z-index: var(--z-dropdown)`, eating every click. Row 2 sits below the panel, which is precisely the reported asymmetry. The panel shows almost always, since `getSelectedCellFormat` returns 1 cell for a plain caret.

The **uncommitted working-tree diff already fixes this** — it adds `computeTableToolbarStackPosition()` which measures placement against the combined toolbar+panel height and returns an explicit `cellRowTop`. Finish it, plus one hardening change:

- `TABLE_TOOLBAR_IDEAL_HEIGHT` (112) and the new `TABLE_CELL_FORMAT_PANEL_HEIGHT` (68) are **hardcoded guesses, never measured**. A font, zoom, or button-wrap difference re-creates the exact overlap. Keep them as the first-paint estimate, then after render measure the real element (`[data-floating-table-toolbar]`) with `getBoundingClientRect()` and recompute. Otherwise this bug comes back on someone else's machine.

### b. "Can't get rid of the table" — reachability, not a missing feature

`deleteTable` exists and works (`table-format.ts:502-507`, dispatched at `:614-615`). It's simply **unreachable**:

- It's the last of 12 text-labelled buttons in a `flex min-w-max` row (`floating-table-toolbar.tsx:315`) inside a container capped at `TABLE_TOOLBAR_IDEAL_WIDTH = 760` with `overflow-x-auto`. At ~90-110px per label the row is 1100px+, so "Delete table" sits off the right edge behind a horizontal scroll nobody discovers.

Two changes:

1. **Register the missing commands.** Add the three definitions to `src/utils/editor-commands.ts` with `availability: "table"`, alongside the existing table entries. Wiring is nearly free — `TABLE_COMMAND_MAP` in `twyne-editor.tsx:92-97` just needs three more lines (`"table.delete-row": "deleteRow"`, etc.); the executor cases already exist at `:2393`, `:2402`, `:2417`. 2. **Pin the destructive cluster in the toolbar.** Pull `deleteRow` / `deleteColumn` / `deleteTable` out of the scrolling row into a trailing group with `sticky right-0` and a paper background, so they stay visible regardless of horizontal scroll position. ## 3. Theming

### Why this is cheap here

| | |
|---|---|
| `var(--color-*)` call sites in TSX | **1873** |
| Tailwind color utilities / arbitrary hex in TSX | **0** |
| Raw hex literals in TSX | 13 (7 files) |
| Tokens covering ~90% of usage | **7** (`--color-paper`, `-2`, `-3`, `-soft`, `--color-ink`, `-light`, `-muted`) + `--color-vermilion` |

Tokens live in a Tailwind v4 `@theme` block at `src/global.css:13-63`. There is no `tailwind.config.*` — the entire Tailwind setup is the Vite plugin. There is **no** existing theme support: `prefers-color-scheme`, `data-theme`, `.dark`, `darkMode`, `ThemeProvider`, `useTheme` all return zero matches repo-wide.

### The one real obstacle: baked-in rgba

103 `rgba()` literals in `global.css` hardcode the palette into textures — paper grain (`:85-100`), `.folio` shadows (`:423-431`), `.ink-bleed` (`:1763`), `.paper-sheet` foxing (`:1643`). On a different ground these invert wrongly (a white inset highlight on dark paper reads as a scratch).

But they're highly concentrated, and the fix is mechanical:

| literal | count | becomes |
|---|---|---|
| `rgba(31, 27, 22, α)` | **52** | `color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-ink) α%, transparent)` |
| `rgba(255, 255, 255, α)` | 10 | `var(--emboss-highlight)` (new token) |
| `rgba(193, 39, 45, α)` | 9 | `color-mix(… var(--color-vermilion) …)` |
| `rgba(92, 107, 192, α)` | 6 | `color-mix(… var(--color-periwinkle) …)` |

77 of 103 map to four tokens. `color-mix` is already the house idiom — 15 uses in `global.css`, plus 7 TSX files including `floating-table-toolbar.tsx`.

1. **`src/utils/theme.ts`** (new). `ThemePreference = { preset: ThemePresetId; custom?: Partial<Record<ThemeTokenId, string>> }`; `THEME_PRESETS`; `readThemePreference()` / `writeThemePreference()`; `applyTheme(pref, root)` stamping `data-theme` plus `style.setProperty` for custom overrides; `contrastRatio(a, b)` for the WCAG guard. 3. **Tokenize the textures** per the table above; add `--emboss-highlight`, `--grain-ink`, `--ink-bleed-shadow`, `--folio-shadow`.
4. **Define the 3 missing tokens.** `--color-accent` (21 uses), `--color-rule` (2), `--color-crimson` (1) are referenced but **defined nowhere** — currently rendering as `unset`. Same for 10 phantom `cssVar`s named in `src/utils/palette.ts`. Fix while in the file.

6. **`router-head.tsx:67`** — `<meta name="theme-color" content="#9c1a1f">` is hardcoded; make it theme-reactive.
7. **Settings → Appearance.** New `<section class="folio p-5">` in `src/routes/settings/index.tsx` (9 sections today, none for appearance). Preset picker + collapsible custom palette over the 8 core tokens, reusing `src/components/ui/color-picker.tsx`. Apply to `document.documentElement` **immediately on change**, not on next mount — the precedent and its rationale are at `personas-panel.tsx:1460-1477`. Show the WCAG ink-on-paper ratio with a warning under 4.5:1.

Add an `appearance` key to the `roomSettings` blob — `convex/schema.ts:163-168` types it `v.any()`, so **no migration**. On load, local wins for first paint; reconcile from remote afterwards only when remote `updatedAt` is newer.

## The page-gap bug

Your instinct about headings was right, and the mechanism is specific. In `paginate()`, the backwards `keepWithNext` walk that protects headings is bounded by `breakAt > runStart + 1`. When a heading is immediately followed by a paragraph taller than one page, that guard is *already* false — so the walk can't move, and the run closes with **nothing on the sheet but the heading**. Repeat per long paragraph, and you get the trail of near-empty pages.

The deeper cause is that blocks are atomic: a paragraph taller than the content box bleeds across sheets *wherever* it starts, so pushing it to a fresh page bought no fidelity and cost the tail of the page before it. Now an unfittable block starts where it falls and bleeds from there; only the block after it takes a break. Guarded on the run so far actually fitting, so the degenerate case (margins dragged until they meet) still falls back to one block per sheet instead of one unbounded run.

Two regression tests cover it, including `a heading is never marooned on a blank page by the paragraph it opens`.

**On your two suggestions:** horizontal margins already exist and are applied (`--doc-pad-left/right`) — they're just tight, 2rem ≈ 0.33in against a typical 1in. And I did *not* remove the heading break rule: it's what stops a heading being stranded at the bottom of a page, and it mirrors `break-after: avoid` in the print stylesheet. The stranding was the guard misfiring, not the guard being wrong.

**What I can't fix within this engine:** text genuinely drifting mid-paragraph across a boundary. Splitting a paragraph would mean fragmenting a block with decorations, which is the documented ceiling of a ProseMirror decoration engine — `pagination-geometry.ts:230` spells out why. Every browser-based word processor has the same limit. The gaps are gone; a single >1-page paragraph will still flow across the seam.
